summary: Earnings season is the main event risk: MCO reported a miss this morning, WDFC and VRSN/SAM sit at the front of the calendar, and a cluster of names (DORM, EXLS, INCY, LOGI, then CALX, CVS, GRMN, RRC) reports within 3 to 5 trading days. All earnings dates are approximate (last year + 364 days). Company-specific news is otherwise mostly analyst price-target changes; the macro tape is dominated by AI/data-center fragility (Fink recession warning, SOX streak), a 5.14% 10-year yield and Iran/Hormuz headlines. L1 (stop anchoring) is for the proposer and PM, so it did not shape this note.

notable.headline: Moody's Q3 Adj. EPS $4.14 Misses $4.26 Estimate, Sales $2.023B Miss $2.077B; FY26 guidance affirmed
notable.read: A double miss on the day the earnings flag expired, softened by affirmed guidance. The fiscal.ai summary ties the weakness to a leveraged-debt slowdown. Guidance sits slightly below consensus on adjusted EPS ($16.50-$17.00 vs $16.93 midpoint-ish).

notable.headline: Jefferies Adjusts Price Target on Tapestry to $125 From $144
notable.read: A second PT cut in two days after UBS cut to $200 from $232 on 10-20, and Jefferies' cut is much larger (-13%) with a PT well below UBS's. Two cuts in a row ahead of 11-05 earnings is a developing negative drift in sell-side sentiment, not a one-off.

notable.headline: Guggenheim Maintains Buy on Kroger, Raises PT to $68; Bloomberg: Kroger to invest $5B on lowering prices
notable.read: Continues the 10-20 investor-day story (7%-11% EPS CAGR through 2029, FY26 guide reaffirmed). Guggenheim's raise is supportive, but the $5B price investment is a margin trade-off that the sell side will have to weigh. The 10-17 grocery-chain cyber incident is still unattributed. The 'Cheese Tax' song lawsuit is trivial.

notable.headline: JPMorgan raises PT to $710; Morgan Stanley to $671; RBC reiterates Outperform $655
notable.read: Post-earnings analyst follow-through after the 10-20 beat. Supportive, but a wide spread in targets and a stock that already reacted; not a new fundamental fact.

notable.headline: Loop downgrade to Hold ($330), MoffettNathanson Neutral PT $283, Oct 28 event, earnings date unclear
notable.read: Two catalysts in the next 8 trading days with the sell side turning more cautious into them, offset by strong iPhone Duo demand (82-day lead time) and the Russia tariff waiver. The earnings date discrepancy (10-29 vs 11-02) matters for sizing around the window.

notable.headline: Larry Fink Warns Data Center Slowdown Could Push US Into 'Recession' as Trump Orders Facilities to Generate Their Own Power
notable.read: Adds a policy and cost angle to the fragile AI/data-center complex flagged yesterday (SOX 8-day streak, AI IPO -32%, midterm polling risk). Meta and Tesla earnings this week add index-level event risk.

notable.headline: CFTC chair says proposed rules could allow US retail crypto margin up to 7x; JPMorgan projects 10% annualized BTC returns; SpaceX holds all its BTC
notable.read: Mostly constructive (leverage access and institutional validation), though 7x retail leverage is also a future volatility amplifier. BTC is around $82-83k after a ~6% correction with weak spot demand and ETF inflows recovering ($526.6M on 10-19/20). No exchange failures or new adverse regulatory action. Continues the CLARITY Act politics thread from yesterday.

notable.headline: Ethereum, Solana staking at record levels but yields falling (Bitwise); JPM Coin on Ethereum
notable.read: Structurally positive adoption news, with falling staking yield a minor offset. No risk event.

notable.headline: Deficit warnings; 10-year yield 5.14%; Fed Chair Warsh rate-hike odds
notable.read: Nothing new today beyond yesterday's duration-sleeve risk (TLT/IEF/BND/VNQ), though the 10-20 headlines that oil and yields cooled helped risk assets. Hike odds and the $110 Brent backdrop persist. A quiet day for rate-specific news.
